name: Document versions, expiry and replacement on published pages
scope: Set an expiration date in the Expires field on each document your client withdraws or limits in time, so users without administrator permissions cannot publish it and the background job that runs every day at midnight by default removes it from Publish; unpublish at once any document that cannot wait for that run. Where your client's teams use the Experience Manager desktop app or Adobe Asset Link, apply the setting that keeps expired assets out of browsing and search there too. Upload each approved replacement under the existing asset's name and folder and keep it as a new version, check the pages its References tab lists before publishing, and if the replacement is wrong, revert to the previous version in the Timeline and publish it again.
evidence: Uploading an asset with the same path ... as an existing asset triggers a warning dialog that presents three resolution options ... A new version of the existing asset is created in the repository, preserving the earlier state so no work is lost. You can view the two versions in the Timeline and can revert to the previously existing version if necessary.

other_pages.quote: Adobe Experience Manager enables Digital Asset Management (DAM) users to check all references to an asset across webpages. The References tab in an asset’s Properties page lists both the local and remote references of the asset, providing a single, consolidated view of where the asset is used.

hours_reasoning: Compared with AS04 Processing profiles and renditions (16/32/64), AS05 Content Hub portal for approved assets (16/32/64) and XG04 Approved assets and filters for creators (16/32/64), which also checks expiry dates. Settings, a runbook and tests with editors, with one repository setting and no other code, so the same band; low is one site and a short withdrawal list, high is a long list across several sites and editor groups.
ext: AEM Sites for the pages that use the documents
notes: Written for AEM Assets as a Cloud Service in the Assets console, where Adobe's pages put the Expires field, the References tab and the Timeline, with the pages built in AEM Sites. Adobe's Manage assets page says the Experience Manager interface keeps expired assets out of browsing and search, while its Digital Rights Management page shows them flagged Expired in the card and list views; the author account test in the last step shows what an author sees. On Edge Delivery sites that place Dynamic Media with OpenAPI assets by reference, Adobe says the reference helps carry expiry, deletion and updates through to the pages; that picker, delivery and publishing sit with AXD05, AXD06 and AXD07. Where pages use the document from a remote DAM through Connected Assets, Adobe says Sites authors preview the updates and then republish the changes to make them available on the publish instance, so the runbook republishes each page listed under Remote References. XC01 (Sites to a remote AEM Assets environment through Dynamic Media with OpenAPI) and XC02 (image modifiers) are not part of this service. Boundaries: AS01 (users and access) and AS04 (renditions) do not touch this work; AS02 designs the folders, tags and metadata forms (fields such as model, revision and language belong there), AS03 moves the library in, AS05 releases approved assets to Content Hub, AS06 is the monthly administration, XG04 checks expiry dates for GenStudio creators, XJ20 and XJ21 deploy Adobe Asset Link and the desktop app (this service only turns on hiding expired assets there), and XJ22 teaches creatives when to check out. Not included: changing when Adobe's expiry job runs or turning on its emails (com.day.cq.dam.core.impl.ExpiryNotificationJobImpl, an OSGi file committed to the Cloud Manager Git repository); the job removes expired assets from Publish every day at midnight by default, so the runbook unpublishes urgent withdrawals at once. The runbook uses new versions and never Replace, which gives the asset a new ID and deletes its metadata and annotations.

steps: Agree with your document owners which documents carry an expiry date and who approves replacements, and write the runbook: replacements keep the document's name and folder, as new versions.
List each withdrawn document's pages on its References tab, agree each page's change with its owner, then set the Expires field and unpublish urgent withdrawals at once.
Run the first replacements with your editors: upload each as a new version, check its pages on the References tab, publish, then test a revert in the Timeline and republish.
Hide expired assets in the desktop app and Adobe Asset Link where you use them, and test with an author account that expired documents cannot be found or published.
deliverables: Expiry dates on the agreed documents
First replacements, published and checked page by page
Test results for expiry, hiding and revert
asks: A document owner who approves each replacement and each withdrawal
The list of documents to withdraw or limit in time, with their end dates
A few editors for the first replacements and the tests
method.risk: A document withdrawn while pages still link to it: we list those pages on its References tab first, and each owner agrees the page's change before the expiry date.
method.outcome: Each approved replacement is published as a new version once its pages are checked, a wrong one can be reverted and republished, and expired documents leave your public site.

phrases: replace a document on every page
expired documents removed from the website
find pages affected by a replacement document
checker_changes: All quotes were refetched today (curl, browser User-Agent) and checked with lib.py has(): each is FOUND word for word on its page.

Quote: the DRM entry 'The expiry information ensures that the published asset is automatically unpublished when it expires.' is replaced by Adobe's sentence on the background job that removes expired assets from Publish and runs every day at midnight by default, quoted without its closing full stop, which follows a tag on the page (FOUND only that way).

Scope sentence 1: the expiry now names that job and its midnight default run, and a document that cannot wait for the run is unpublished at once (the page says that when a published asset's date is moved earlier, the scheduler detects it as expired when it next runs).
Method step 2: lists each withdrawn document's pages, then sets the Expires field and unpublishes urgent withdrawals at once (27 words).

Notes: 'Adobe's expiry email scheduler' was wrong, since that job is the one that unpublishes and it emails only when email notification is enabled; the sentence now leaves out changing when the job runs or turning on its emails, and says the runbook unpublishes urgent withdrawals at once.

Quotes: no quote carried 'unpublish at once' (scope sentence 1, method step 2), so a Manage assets entry now quotes 'Select the Publish or Unpublish option as required. ... Select Now to act on the asset immediately.'; to keep five other pages, the DRM sentence on users without administrator permissions joined the Expires field entry ahead of that sentence, in page order, with an ellipsis.

Evidence: now starts with Adobe's condition for a new version, an upload with the same path as an existing asset (the ellipses skip the em-dashed 'identical name and location' and the list of the three options); FOUND.

Scope sentence 3: each replacement is uploaded under the existing asset's name and folder as a new version, since an upload under a new name is a separate asset, and a reverted version is published again, since a revert changes only the author copy.
Method step 1: the runbook now says replacements keep the document's name and folder, as new versions (29 words).
Method step 3: the first replacements are published, and the revert test ends by republishing (30 words).

Outcome: no longer claims a published replacement reaches every page that references the document, which no quote carried, and for pages that use Connected Assets Adobe says Sites authors republish the changes to make them available; it now says what the work delivers (29 words).

Notes: added the Connected Assets boundary (Adobe says Sites authors preview the updates and then republish the changes, Adobe's 'the changes' kept rather than 'the pages'; the runbook republishes each page under Remote References) and that XC01 and XC02, the two services on the Sites and Assets connection, are not part of this service.

Phrases: 'restore the previous version of a document', 'find pages affected by a document change' and 'where a document is used' became 'recover the superseded document', 'find pages affected by a replacement document' and 'asset expiration and automatic unpublishing'; with the matcher's own phraseScore, AS07 still leads B.3 (21.40) and B.2 (19.51), now leads an asset expiration ask (15.83), and no longer leads a page restore or a template change ask.
Left as it is: 'roll back a replacement document' still wins a page rollback ask (6.19) because no AEM Sites service has a rollback phrase; that belongs in SI07's phrases, not this file.
